## REQ-CNT-001

**Platform provides the Message Bus storage**

The platform maps a host-defined path, mounted read-only, to the target path /etc/oi4/mqtt of every container. The Message Bus storage contains at least broker.pem (public certificate of the broker), broker.json (settings of the broker, REQ-CNT-003) and, if the broker certificate was signed by a local CA other than the CA of ca.pem in the OI4 certificate storage (REQ-CNT-005), broker_ca.pem (that CA); otherwise clients verify the broker certificate against ca.pem.

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform
- Refs: RIG 4.1.1, SF-091
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.1-078a70a1, RIG-4.1.1-15bd8eb6, RIG-4.1.1-723b5b51, RIG-4.1.1-e577eb27

> The Message Bus storage shall be used to make the public certificate and the settings of the MQTT broker available to the container and their MQTT clients.
> — RIG 4.1.1

> The target path is the path inside the container, which must be mapped to a host-defined path inside the host system.
> — RIG 4.1.1

> The host path shall be mounted read only!
> — RIG 4.1.1

> The Message Bus storage shall contain at least the following files:
> — RIG 4.1.1

Notes: broker_ca.pem is present only for a local CA other than the CA of ca.pem (RIG 4.1.1 since SF-091 (a), guideline fbe6173). With REQ-CNT-005 a CA certificate for the verification of the broker certificate (REQ-MQTT-008) is always available. The broker address in broker.json is also required by REQ-MQTT-003. Back to draft in the C-030 review (SF-091 revised 2026-10-22).

## REQ-CNT-002

**No private keys in the Message Bus and certificate storages**

The platform stores no private keys in the Message Bus storage (/etc/oi4/mqtt) and in the OI4 certificate storage (/etc/oi4/certs); private keys are provided via the secret storage (REQ-CNT-008).

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform
- Refs: RIG 4.1.1, RIG 4.1.2
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.1-c7dae7e5, RIG-4.1.2-f09704cd

> Folder which contains the MQTT settings and the public certificate of the broker HIGHLY RECOMMENDED Do not store any private keys here!
> — RIG 4.1.1

> Storage for certificates. Such as the certificates of the applications (see 4.1.3 Secret Storage) and CA certificate to validate other certificates. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED Do not store any private keys here!
> — RIG 4.1.2

## REQ-CNT-003

**Content of broker.json**

broker.json in the Message Bus storage is a JSON object with the mandatory fields Address (String, IP address or host name of the broker), SecurePort (UINT16, port on which the broker listens for TLS connections) and MaxPacketSize (INT32, maximum size of an MQTT payload in bytes, at least 262144 and at most 268435455). The broker accepts payloads up to MaxPacketSize.

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform, broker
- Refs: RIG 4.1.1, MG 6.2.1, SF-091
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.1-516de8c7, RIG-4.1.1-58d0cc4a, RIG-4.1.1-bf0c6b45

> broker.json JSON coded file containing the settings of the MQTT broker.
> — RIG 4.1.1

> Defines the maximum size of a MQTT payload in bytes.
> — RIG 4.1.1

> The minimum value of MaxPacketSize is 262144 (256 KiB)
> — RIG 4.1.1

> The intention of the MaxPacketSize is to protect the Message Bus broker and client.
> — RIG 4.1.1

Notes: That the broker accepts payloads up to MaxPacketSize follows from the purpose of the field (publishers may use the full size, REQ-PAG-005). The upper bound 268435455 (maximum remaining length of an MQTT v3.1.1 packet) replaced "INT32max" with SF-091 (b) (guideline fbe6173). A JSON Schema of broker.json can be added with D8.

## REQ-CNT-004

**Application uses the Message Bus storage**

A containerized application takes the broker address (Address), the port (SecurePort) and the MaxPacketSize from /etc/oi4/mqtt/broker.json and verifies the broker certificate with broker_ca.pem or, if not present, with the CA of the OI4 certificate storage; it needs no other configuration of these settings.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 none · L2 SHOULD · L3 MUST
- Domain: service-container · Applies to: application, container-image
- Refs: RIG 4.1.1, RIG 1.3
- Verification: d8, manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.1-723b5b51

> The Message Bus storage shall be used to make the public certificate and the settings of the MQTT broker available to the container and their MQTT clients.
> — RIG 4.1.1

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-029. The client side of the messaging domain already requires the port (REQ-MQTT-004), the certificate verification (REQ-MQTT-008) and a NetworkMessage within MaxPacketSize (REQ-PAG-005) at every messaging level.

## REQ-CNT-005

**Platform always provides a CA certificate in the certificate storage**

The platform provides the OI4 certificate storage /etc/oi4/certs (REQ-CNT-006) to every container, with ca.pem: the certificate of the CA used to validate certificates. If the broker certificate was not signed by this CA, the CA that signed it is provided as broker_ca.pem (REQ-CNT-001). Every container can thus verify the broker certificate (REQ-MQTT-008).

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform
- Refs: RIG 4.1.2, RIG 4.1.1, MG 6.2.2, SF-035, SF-091
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.2-1d32cac8, RIG-4.1.2-70fa2141, RIG-4.1.2-f5aa1987

> The platform shall make the certificate of the certificate authority (CA) used to validate certificates, in particular the broker certificate (OEC Messaging Guideline, 6.2.2 Security Settings), and the certificates of the applications available by storing them as follows:
> — RIG 4.1.2

> An own CA of the platform is only required if the platform issues certificates, e.g. the certificates of the applications.
> — RIG 4.1.2

> The client must verify the broker certificate when it establishes the TLS connection: the certificate chain against the CA certificate (broker_ca.pem of the Message Bus storage or, if no local CA is present, the CA of the OI4 certificate storage; for a client without container, its configured CA) and the broker address.
> — MG 6.2.2

Notes: TLS is mandatory (REQ-MQTT-005/006) and every client must verify the broker certificate against broker_ca.pem or ca.pem (REQ-MQTT-008, MUST at every level); without a CA certificate no containerized client could connect. Implicit MUST per SF-091 (c)/(g) (C-030 review, 2026-10-22), explicit "shall" in RIG 4.1.2 since guideline fbe6173 (before: "In case the system provides a CA … should"); the first draft was SHOULD with a condition. ca.pem may be a well-known (public) or a platform-specific CA; an own CA that issues certificates is only needed for client certificates and certificates of the applications (REQ-CNT-007).

## REQ-CNT-006

**Content and mount of the certificate storage**

The platform maps a host-defined path, mounted read-only, to the target path /etc/oi4/certs of every container. The OI4 certificate storage contains at least ca.pem (CA for the validation of certificates) and, for a container with a certificate, the certificate of its application (REQ-CNT-007).

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform
- Refs: RIG 4.1.2, SF-091
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.2-54831f39, RIG-4.1.2-9e0b30f0, RIG-4.1.2-aff2fc7b, RIG-4.1.2-e191918f

> The target path is the path inside the Docker container, which must be mapped to a host-defined path inside the host system.
> — RIG 4.1.2

> The host path shall be mounted read only!
> — RIG 4.1.2

> The certificate storage shall contain at least the following files:
> — RIG 4.1.2

> ca.pem CA used for validation of certificates.
> — RIG 4.1.2

Notes: The storage is always provided (REQ-CNT-005, SF-091 (c) revised in the C-030 review; before: conditional), its content "shall"; the certificate of the application is only needed if the application uses it, e.g. for client certificate authentication (REQ-MQTT-009/010) or the other uses of REQ-CNT-025 (GL-ADR-022).

## REQ-CNT-007

**Certificate of the application named after the container**

The certificate of the application of a container (its identity, with the private key in the secret storage, REQ-CNT-008) is stored in the OI4 certificate storage as &lt;containername>.pem, with the container name of RIG 4.2.

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform
- Condition: The application of the container has a certificate.
- Refs: RIG 4.1.2, RIG 4.2, GL-ADR-022
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.2-7bd3e5d6

> &lt;containername>.pem Certificate of a specific application (its identity, see 4.1.3 Secret Storage) should be named as described in 4.2 Container Name Conventions.
> — RIG 4.1.2

Notes: Called "client certificate" until GL-ADR-022; the certificate is the identity of the application for all its uses (REQ-CNT-025).

## REQ-CNT-008

**Platform provides the secrets of the identity of the application**

The platform makes the secrets of the identity of the application of a container available in the secret storage /run/secrets/oi4, mapped from a host-defined path and mounted read-only: credentials (base64(&lt;username>:&lt;password>)), private_key.pem (PEM-encoded private key of the certificate of the application, &lt;containername>.pem in the OI4 certificate storage, REQ-CNT-007) and, if the key is encrypted, passphrase (base64-encoded passphrase). Each file is present only if used; at least one means of authentication is provided – the credentials or the private key together with the certificate. The folder contains only these files; further secrets of the application are provided outside of it.

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform
- Refs: RIG 4.1.3, MG 6.2.2, GL-ADR-022
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.3-04e70172, RIG-4.1.3-0b3ec5ba, RIG-4.1.3-2494f946, RIG-4.1.3-3ccf87cc

> In an Open Industry 4.0 Alliance-compliant platform, the secrets of the identity of an application shall be made available to its container under the following paths:
> — RIG 4.1.3

> The platform shall provide at least one means of authentication: the credentials or the private key together with the certificate of the application.
> — RIG 4.1.3

> The target path is the path inside the Docker container, which must be mapped to a host-defined path inside the host system.
> — RIG 4.1.3

> The host path shall be mounted read only!
> — RIG 4.1.3

> The folder /run/secrets/oi4 is reserved for the files of Table 7.
> — RIG 4.1.3

Notes: GL-ADR-022 (PO order 2026-10-22) replaced /run/secrets/mqtt_credentials, mqtt_private_key.pem and mqtt_passphrase by the folder /run/secrets/oi4 and resolved SF-091 (d) (addressee platform, at least one means of authentication). The usernames follow REQ-MQTT-011.

## REQ-CNT-009

**Application uses the certificate and secret storages**

A containerized application takes the secrets of its identity from /run/secrets/oi4: the username and password by base64-decoding credentials and splitting at the first ":", the private key of its certificate from private_key.pem (decrypted with the base64-decoded passphrase, if present) and its certificate from /etc/oi4/certs/&lt;containername>.pem. It uses them for the authentication at the Message Bus and needs no other configuration of these secrets.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 none · L2 SHOULD · L3 MUST
- Domain: service-container · Applies to: application, container-image
- Refs: RIG 4.1.3, RIG 4.1.2, RIG 1.3, MG 6.2.2, GL-ADR-022
- Verification: d8, manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.3-7745248f, RIG-4.1.3-fabb06b7

> To obtain the username and the password, the application shall decode the content of credentials (base64) and split the result at the first colon (:).
> — RIG 4.1.3

> The username does not contain a colon (OEC Messaging Guideline, 6.2.2 Security Settings), the password may contain colons.
> — RIG 4.1.3

> With this identity, the application authenticates itself at the Message Bus (OEC Messaging Guideline, 6.2.2 Security Settings).
> — RIG 4.1.3

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-029 (secret handling). Which means is used if both are available: REQ-MQTT-010. The decoding is explicit since GL-ADR-022 (SF-091 (d)); a username contains no ":" (REQ-MQTT-011).

## REQ-CNT-010

**Application uses the OI4 application storage paths**

If the system provides a persistent layer, a containerized application that needs persistent configuration or data stores its configuration in /etc/oi4/app and its data in /opt/oi4/app.

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 none · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: service-container · Applies to: application, container-image
- Condition: The system provides a persistent layer and the application needs persistent configuration or data.
- Refs: RIG 4.1.4, SF-091
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.4-a5f1c4d1, RIG-4.1.4-b206a9a5, RIG-4.1.4-ffa2fd84

> In case the system provides a persistent layer, the application should use the following paths to make use of it.
> — RIG 4.1.4

> /etc/oi4/app Storage for application specific configuration
> — RIG 4.1.4

> /opt/oi4/app Storage for application specific data
> — RIG 4.1.4

Notes: The paths are recommended (SF-091 (e)); the table said "shall be stored here" until guideline fbe6173.

## REQ-CNT-011

**Application storages are mapped and owned by one container**

If the platform provides a persistent layer, it maps a host-defined path to /etc/oi4/app and /opt/oi4/app of a container; only this one container has access to its own application specific volume.

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform
- Condition: The platform provides a persistent layer.
- Refs: RIG 4.1.4, SF-091
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.4-4d7c9a08, RIG-4.1.4-9177c92c

> The target paths /etc/oi4/app and /opt/oi4/app are paths inside the Docker container, which must be mapped to a host-defined path inside the host system.
> — RIG 4.1.4

> Attention must be paid to access permissions; to guarantee the data ownership, only one container shall have access to its own application specific volume.
> — RIG 4.1.4

Notes: The host mapping does not apply to /opt/oi4/licenses (REQ-CNT-017, SF-091 (e); stated in the RIG 4.1.4 note since guideline fbe6173).

## REQ-CNT-012

**Application detects manipulation of its stored data**

A containerized application takes measures to detect manipulation of the data in its application specific storages and protects it (e.g. by encryption) if necessary.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 none · L2 SHOULD · L3 MUST
- Domain: service-container · Applies to: application
- Condition: The application uses an application specific storage.
- Refs: RIG 4.1.4
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.4-4d2eb4a9

> Because container volumes are not protected against external access to read/write in general, the application has to take measures to detect data manipulation and might protect it (e.g. encryption) if necessary.
> — RIG 4.1.4

Notes: Graded by REQ-CMP-029.

## REQ-CNT-013

**SBOM in /opt/oi4/licenses**

A containerized application provides a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) describing the licenses of all its software components in the folder /opt/oi4/licenses: either SPDX (ISO/IEC 5962:2021) as sbom.spdx.json or CycloneDX (ECMA-424) as sbom.cdx.json, each in the JSON serialization of the format. Exactly one of these two files is present.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 none · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: service-container · Applies to: container-image
- Refs: RIG 4.1.4, RIG 4, RIG 1.3, RIG 5.2, GL-ADR-002
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4-686e2ed9, RIG-4.1.4-0a58da0d, RIG-4.1.4-0b9c4e0b, RIG-4.1.4-97a172ef, RIG-4.1.4-d208c6fb, RIG-4.1.4-e49f19d5, RIG-5.2-1b1e9b90

> Instead, every Open Industry 4.0 Alliance-compliant application shall provide this information in the folder /opt/oi4/licenses.
> — RIG 4.1.4

> The licenses of all software components used in the application shall be described in a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) in one of the following formats:
> — RIG 4.1.4

> The SBOM shall use the JSON serialization of the selected format and shall be stored with a canonical file name, so that it can be detected without further configuration:
> — RIG 4.1.4

> Exactly one of these SBOM files shall be present.
> — RIG 4.1.4

> The license and SBOM storage (4.1.4 Application Specific Storages) is mandatory from Level 2 on.
> — RIG 4

Notes: Detail of REQ-CMP-028 (reviewed umbrella).

## REQ-CNT-014

**License texts in the SBOM or as &lt;License-ID>.txt**

Every license text is either part of the SBOM or stored as /opt/oi4/licenses/&lt;License-ID>.txt, where &lt;License-ID> is the SPDX license identifier of the license or the LicenseRef- identifier used in the SBOM for a license without SPDX identifier.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 none · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: service-container · Applies to: container-image
- Refs: RIG 4.1.4, RIG 1.3, GL-ADR-002
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed

## REQ-CNT-019

**Unique container name set as hostname**

When a container is created, the platform assigns it a well-defined container name that is unique within the OEC platform, has at most 63 characters and follows the host name rules of RFC 1123 (letters, digits and hyphens only), and sets the container hostname to this name.

- Keyword: MUST
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform
- Refs: RIG 4.2, SF-090
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.2-36a1dde9, RIG-4.2-75e6ea8e, RIG-4.2-997b0f1d, RIG-4.2-f4e41f77

> Each OI4 Alliance-compliant container shall have a well-defined name for identification.
> — RIG 4.2

> To meet these requirements, the container name must be unique within the Open Edge Computing platform, while also not exceeding 63 characters.
> — RIG 4.2

> The platform assigns the container name when the container is created and shall make it available to the container by setting the container hostname.
> — RIG 4.2

> The RFC 1123 rules for assigning a host name must also be followed for container names so that DNS resolution works correctly: letters, digits and hyphens only.
> — RIG 4.2

Notes: SF-090 (b), (c) resolved: "unique within the Open Edge Computing platform" (before: "globally unique according to the definition of the OI4 Alliance") and the platform as addressee. Back to draft in the C-030 closure (uniqueness scope changed).

## REQ-CNT-020

**Container name with a UUID postfix**

The container name consists of a self-defined default container name of at most 26 characters with a UUID as postfix, separated by a hyphen (&lt;DefaultContainerName>-&lt;uuid>), so that several instances never get the same name and the name is unique beyond the platform as well.

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform
- Refs: RIG 4.2, SF-090
- Verification: d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.2-21db7fba, RIG-4.2-7935e203

> Best practice is to use a naming scheme such as &lt;DefaultContainerName>-&lt;uuid>; the UUID also makes the container name unique beyond the platform.
> — RIG 4.2

> With a UUID of 36 characters and the separator, the &lt;DefaultContainerName> has at most 26 characters.
> — RIG 4.2

> To avoid several instances of a container with the same container name, it is best practice to use a UUID as postfix on top of a self-defined container name such as &lt;DefaultContainerName>-&lt;uuid>.
> — RIG 4.2

Notes: SF-090 (a), (e) resolved: separator "-" instead of "_" (RFC 1123), at most 26 characters for the default container name. Back to draft in the C-030 closure (separator changed).

## REQ-CNT-021

**Application uses its container name**

A containerized application determines its container name from its hostname and uses it as name of its certificate (REQ-CNT-007) and, if it uses the Oi4Identifier as Identification Link, as SerialNumber in the Oi4Identifier.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 none · L2 SHOULD · L3 MUST
- Domain: service-container · Applies to: application
- Refs: RIG 4.2, MG 4.3.1, RIG 1.3, SF-090
- Verification: manual, d8
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.2-9b5221a1

> The application shall determine its container name from its hostname and shall use it as follows:
> — RIG 4.2

> As the name of the certificate of the application (4.1.2 OI4 Certificate Storage)
> — RIG 4.2

> As a serial number inside the Oi4Identifier (OEC Messaging Guideline, 4.3 The Oi4Identifier), if the Oi4Identifier is used as Identification Link and thus as AppId (OEC Messaging Guideline, 7.3 AppId Element)
> — RIG 4.2

> When deploying a container which by its nature has no serial number and can be instantiated multiple times, use the container name as SerialNumber as defined in OEC Runtime & Infrastructure Guideline, 4.2 Container Name Conventions.
> — MG 4.3.1

Notes: SF-090 (d) resolved: explicit "shall" (before: implicit MUST). The MQTT ClientId is no longer part of this requirement: RIG 4.2 now refers to the recommendation of MG 6.2.3 (REQ-MQTT-013, SHOULD at all levels). Graded by REQ-CMP-029. Back to draft in the C-030 closure (ClientId removed, no longer implicit).

## REQ-CNT-022

**Digest where an immutable image version is needed**

Container images are referenced by tag by default. Where a dedicated, immutable version of an image is needed (e.g. the same image on several edge computers), the image is referenced by its digest (SHA256).

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 none · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: service-container · Applies to: container-image, platform
- Condition: A dedicated, immutable version of the image is needed.
- Refs: RIG 4.3, RIG 3, SF-091
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-3-d124e0fb, RIG-4.3-37a27c8a, RIG-4.3-b9c787bb

> Therefore, the usage of tags within the OI4 Alliance is permitted and the default.
> — RIG 4.3

> In cases where a dedicated, immutable version of an image is needed, digests can be used. A digest is the unique identifier of an image as a SHA256 hash.
> — RIG 4.3

Notes: The only RIG 4.3 statement with a keyword is the recommendation (tip box); REQ-CMP-030 (L3 Mandatory) therefore grades a recommendation, which stays SHOULD at Level 3 (SF-091 (f)). Addressed to whoever installs the image (operator, platform) and to the provider, who publishes the digests.

## REQ-CNT-023

**Bridge network preferred**

A container is attached to a bridge network rather than to the host network, unless it needs low-level Ethernet communication.

- Keyword: SHOULD
- Levels: L1 none · L2 SHOULD · L3 SHOULD
- Domain: service-container · Applies to: container-image, platform
- Refs: RIG 4.4, SF-091
- Verification: d8, manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.4-fbcccae3

> For the use of containers in an OI4 Alliance-compliant Edge Computing environment, the use of bridge network types should be preferred.
> — RIG 4.4

> Low level Ethernet communication is possible.
> — RIG 4.4

Notes: The exception for low-level Ethernet (OT connectors) is derived from the advantage/disadvantage tables (host network, bridge network). REQ-CMP-031 (L3 Mandatory) grades this recommendation, which stays SHOULD at Level 3 (SF-091 (f)).

## REQ-CNT-024

**One secret storage per container**

Every container has its own secret storage; the platform does not make the secret storage of a container available to another container.

- Keyword: MUST NOT
- Domain: platform · Applies to: platform
- Refs: RIG 4.1.3, GL-ADR-022
- Verification: d8, manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.3-c4b8fd9f, RIG-4.1.3-fb9febc6

> Every container has its own secret storage.
> — RIG 4.1.3

> The platform shall not make the secret storage of a container available to another container.
> — RIG 4.1.3

Notes: New with GL-ADR-022: the private key is the identity of one application; the OI4 certificate storage, which holds only public data, may be shared (REQ-CNT-007).

## REQ-CNT-025

**Application may use its identity for other purposes**

Besides the authentication at the Message Bus, an application may use its identity (certificate and secrets, REQ-CNT-008/009) for other purposes, e.g. for signing messages, for the authentication at other systems or as server certificate of a web server (HTTPS) it provides.

- Keyword: MAY
- Levels: L1 none · L2 MAY · L3 MAY
- Domain: service-container · Applies to: application
- Refs: RIG 4.1.3, GL-ADR-022
- Verification: manual
- Status: reviewed
- Inventory: RIG-4.1.3-71d36c2a

> The application may also use its identity for other purposes, e.g. for signing messages, for the authentication at other systems or as server certificate of a web server (HTTPS) that the application provides.
> — RIG 4.1.3

Notes: New with GL-ADR-022. Which purposes a certificate supports depends on its key usage and extended key usage set by the issuer (note in RIG 4.1.3, e.g. serverAuth and the host name for a web server); the guideline does not require the platform to issue such certificates. Levels as the other application uses of the container storages (REQ-CNT-009).
